title: Medication Check Visits on a Refill Day
content:
**Medicaid Managed Care Membership — pharmacy benefit training note: medication check visits**

**What makes a sick visit a medication check?** When primary care office visits are re-rated as preventive or coordinated care, a sick visit the primary care visit log records on the day of the latest maintenance refill the Pharmacy Benefit dispensed is a medication check. The refill day is the fill date of the latest paid fill of fill type refill that the pharmacy benefit shows.

**At what copay does a medication check re-rate?** It re-rates at the medication-check copay set by the practice type of the member's current assignment in the Primary Care Provider Assignment records:

| Current practice type | Medication-check copay |
|---|---|
| Patient-Centered Medical Home Practice | 1.00 USD |
| Federally Qualified Health Center Home | 1.00 USD |
| Any other practice type | 3.00 USD |

**What if no sick visit falls on the latest refill day?** Then nothing is re-rated under this rule.

**Which refill day counts when the member refills several times?** Only the latest paid refill's fill date. A sick visit on the day of an earlier refill, or on the day of a first fill that is not a refill, is not a medication check under this rule.

**Is every sick visit on that day re-rated?** Yes, each sick visit the log records on the latest refill day re-rates at the medication-check copay for the current practice type.

**Hypothetical illustration.** Inputs chosen for illustration only: the Pharmacy Benefit shows paid refills on 5 May and 4 August; a sick visit is logged on 4 August; the current practice is a Health Home Lead Provider, which is not a medical-home practice. The visit is a medication check and re-rates at 3.00. Had the current practice been a Patient-Centered Medical Home Practice, it would re-rate at 1.00.
